verses.text: Then the LORD answered Job out of the storm:
"Who is this who darkens my plans with words that have no knowledge?
Get ready like a man. I will ask you questions, and you will answer me.
Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell me, if you understand.
Who decided how big it would be? Surely you know! Who stretched a measuring line across it?
What were its foundations set on? Who laid its cornerstone,
while the morning stars sang together and all the angels shouted for joy?
Who shut the sea behind doors when it burst out from the womb,
when I made the clouds its clothing and wrapped it in thick darkness,
when I set its limits and put its bars and doors in place,
and said, 'You may come this far, but no farther. Here your proud waves must stop'?
Have you ever in your life given orders to the morning, or shown the dawn its place,
so it could take hold of the edges of the earth and shake the wicked out of it?
The earth takes shape like clay under a seal. Its features stand out like the folds of a garment.
The light is taken away from the wicked, and the arm they raised to strike is broken.
Have you gone down to the springs at the bottom of the sea, or walked in the deepest parts of the ocean?
Have the gates of death been shown to you? Have you seen the gates of the deepest darkness?
Do you understand how wide the earth is? Tell me, if you know all this.
What is the way to the home of light? And where does darkness live?
Can you take them to their places? Do you know the paths to their homes?
Surely you know, because you were already born then, and you have lived so many years!
Have you gone into the storerooms of the snow, or seen the storerooms of the hail,
which I keep for times of trouble, for days of battle and war?
What is the way to the place where the lightning is spread out, or where the east wind is scattered over the earth?
Who cuts a channel for the floodwaters, or a path for the thunderstorm,
to bring rain on land where no one lives, on a wilderness with no people in it,
to water the empty and dry ground and make the new grass grow?
Does the rain have a father? Who is the father of the drops of dew?
Whose womb did the ice come from? Who gave birth to the frost from the sky
when the waters become as hard as stone and the surface of the deep sea freezes?
Can you tie up the star group called the Pleiades, or loosen the belt of Orion?
Can you bring out the star groups in their seasons, or guide the Bear with her cubs?
Do you know the laws of the skies? Can you make them rule over the earth?
Can you shout to the clouds and make them cover you with a flood of water?
Can you send out the lightning bolts so they go? Do they report to you, 'Here we are'?
Who gave wisdom to the heart? Who gave understanding to the mind?
Who is wise enough to count the clouds? Who can tip over the water jars of the sky
when the dust turns hard and the clumps of earth stick together?
Can you hunt food for the lioness, or satisfy the hunger of the young lions
when they crouch in their dens or wait in the bushes?
Who gives food to the raven when its young cry out to God and wander around with nothing to eat?
